title: Is Geothermal Heating and Cooling Worth the Cost?  Heat Pumps Explained
summary: Undecided on geothermal heating and cooling: how ground loops work, loop types, installed cost versus conventional HVAC, savings, payback, lifespan and the 30% federal credit.

assertions.quote: Although the upfront cost of a geothermal system might be higher than a conventional HVAC system
The typical payback and savings in the system is usually around eight to 10 years
They can work well in almost all climates.
around 50 years for the underground infrastructure

verdicts.note: Polyethylene ground loops are rated for 50 years or more while the indoor unit typically lasts about 20 to 25 years.

assertions.quote: provides homeowners a tax credit of 30% from the total installed cost of the Energy Star rated system
simply running when the electricity prices are the lowest
it will produce three to five units of heat for the home
